newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rate cut kicks Australian stocks up at open.
newsitem.headline: Rate cut kicks Australian stocks up at open.

text.p: A surprise interest rate cut kicked the Australian sharemarket higher at the opening on Wednesday with the banks and finance sector leading the way up.

The Reserve Bank of Australia said it had cut official cash rates by 0.5 percent to 6.0 percent citing an improved inflation outlook. From the opening, the All Ordinaries index added 21.2 points to 2,383.0.

"They cut the rates, the market liked it and there was some good turnover early," said broker Robert Cameron of Cameron Securities. The banks and finance index soared 1.9 percent early, compared to early gains in the benchmark All Ordinaries index of about one percent.

"The companies with (dividend) yield have done the best," Cameron said, adding that while the market may have eased from early highs, it could go on with the job in the afternoon as offshore investors digested the rate cut.
"I think you may see some more buying this afternoon."
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about six to one, while about 35 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
